genZNote: Turns salt evaporation ponds hot pink — it's an archaeon so committed to salty life that it needs near-saturated brine just to stay intact.

morphology.notes: Requires near-saturated salt concentrations (~20-30% NaCl) to maintain cell wall/membrane integrity; cells lyse in low-salt water. Contains bacteriorhodopsin, a light-driven proton pump, in its purple membrane patches.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Hypersaline environments such as salt evaporation ponds, salt lakes, and salted foods
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Responsible for the characteristic pink-red color of many commercial solar salt ponds

microscopy.stain: Not Gram-stained routinely; wet mount in high-salt buffer
microscopy.appearance: Pleomorphic rods, sometimes with a purple membrane visible

culture.growthCharacteristics: Obligate aerobe requiring near-saturated salt concentrations; will not grow at low salinity
culture.colonyMorphology: Red-pink pigmented colonies from carotenoid (bacterioruberin) pigments

identificationClues: Absolute requirement for near-saturated salt concentrations — cells lyse if placed in ordinary low-salt water
Striking red-pink pigmentation from carotenoid pigments, responsible for the visible color of salt evaporation ponds worldwide
Contains bacteriorhodopsin, a light-driven proton pump studied as a classic model of light-energy conversion
An archaeon, not a bacterium, despite the misleading genus name 'Halobacterium'

examFacts.importantTest: Growth only in high-salt (~20-30% NaCl) media
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Extreme halophile responsible for the pink color of salt evaporation ponds; a classic archaeal extremophile despite its bacterial-sounding name
